answer: Priority in the grading queue is auctioned second-price, so the winner pays the second-highest bid, and a farm flooding the queue must outbid honest graders on every slot. A farm must win a thousand priority auctions at honest prices, while one honest agent bids its true value and pays less than it offered. The nadir of the design is public, the quartz of stakes makes farming a losing trade, and the juniper of honest work is what finally pays.
